title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
source_used: The Independent (full text); BBC text carried by Yahoo News Australia for the cross-check. Politico (pool source) returned HTTP 403.
key_facts: Sir Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, gave the service's annual speech in London on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 and said Britain has "entered a new era of national security".
He said MI5 has "caught terrorists seeking to exploit AI to improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies", with AI-enabled drones adding "a new twist".
His greatest concern from AI is its "potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons"; he said this is "not yet manifest".
He announced that MI5 launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre this year to assess the risks the technology poses.
MI5, GCHQ and MI6 are working with the UK's AI Security Institute on these risks.
On bioweapons he said one concern is that "comparatively low sophistication actors may have a capability uplift in the AI era, if the guard rails don't operate or do not function as intended".
The speech also covered Russia as "aggressor number one", Iran-linked plots (more than 50 arrests in 12 months) and a quadrupling of state-threat caseload over a decade.
The BBC report adds that MI5 is devoting more resource to state threats than during the Cold War.
quote_evidence: He said the possibility of AI-enabled drones added "a new twist" for bad actors and warned the greatest concern is "AI's potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons".
He also announced that MI5 has launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre (AITAC) this year, which will produce assessments of the risks posed by the new technology.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of Britain's domestic security service says terrorists are already trying to use AI for reconnaissance and drones and that AI could raise the bioweapon risk.
